title: Access controls and SIEM export playbook by environment
content:
Purpose and scope

This playbook describes environment-specific IAM role matrices, canonical policy templates, audit-log schema, and SIEM export mappings for Redwood Inference environments (hosted, dedicated, private). It is intended for security engineers, infra engineers, SREs, and SOC analysts who implement access controls and build evidence automation for audits.

Objectives
- Provide a single reference for how access differs by environment and why.
- Offer ready-to-use policy templates and examples for integration into IaC (Terraform/CloudFormation).
- Define a minimal audit-log schema and examples to ensure consistent ingestion by SIEM.
- Outline evidence automation flows for common compliance requests (SOC2, ISO27001, customer audits).

Environments (high level definitions)
- Hosted: Redwood-managed control plane and inference runtime (multi-tenant). Strict least-privilege for platform components; multi-tenant segregation via tenancy IDs and data tagging.
- Dedicated: Customer-dedicated capacity within Redwood cloud. Control plane managed by Redwood, compute isolated by customer pool. Networking of customer clusters may be dedicated VPCs.
- Private: Customer-owned control plane (VPC/on-prem). Redwood provides software bundle and limited managed services. Customer is responsible for network and host-level controls.

Access model differences (summary)
- Role breadth: Hosted roles are highly scoped (service accounts per microservice + token scopes). Dedicated roles include cluster-owner and pool-ops roles. Private environment surfaces host-level roles (sysadmin equivalents) to customer admins.
- Identity federation: Hosted uses Redwood IdP (okta) with short-lived service tokens. Dedicated offers federated service accounts + customer IdP for admin federation. Private requires customer-managed IdP integration.
- Data access: Hosted prohibits direct host access; data plane access is mediated by Redwood APIs and audited. Dedicated allows controlled API admin access for customer-appointed operators. Private can expose host-level data access; expect customer to certify controls.

RBAC - core roles (canonical matrix)
Note: This is a readable matrix summary; merge into the role documentation tabel in Confluence for the canonical CSV.
- platform-reader: read-only across telemetry and configuration (no secrets).
- platform-operator: manage deployments, scaling, and rollout operations (no secrets unless explicitly granted).
- billing-reader: view usage, cost, and quota (no runtime access).
- model-onboarder: upload and register models, set version metadata, cannot promote to production without canary approver.
- canary-approver: approves rollouts to production clusters. Typically product/security reviewers.
- secret-manager-admin: create and rotate secrets used by runtime. Strictly limited in hosted.
- cluster-admin: full control over nodes and networking (only for private or dedicated with explicit allowlist).
- incident-responder: ephemeral elevated access for incident investigation (timeboxed via Access Requests).

Policy templates (examples)
- Hosted - service principal least-privilege sample (pseudo JSON snippet):
  - actions allowed: ["inference:invoke", "model:read", "metrics:read"]
  - actions denied: ["node:ssh", "secret:write", "billing:write"]
  - resource scoping: ["model:customer:<tenant-id>/*", "namespace:customer:<tenant-id>"]

- Dedicated - operator/admin separation:
  - pool-ops role: manage pool lifecycle, view node health, scale; no secret management unless explicit binding.
  - admin role: cluster-admin + secret-manager-admin (granted only after 2-of-3 approvals).

- Private - customer default template:
  - note: templates intended to be imported by customer IaC; recommend guardrails that map to internal compliance checks (e.g., MFA enforced for admin principals, host access requires approved change request).

Environment-by-environment access rules (detailed guidance)
Hosted:
- No direct SSH/RDP to hosts; all runtime ops go through control-plane APIs and ephemeral exec hooks.
- Service accounts are short-lived (<= 1h) and rotated automatically.
- Secrets accessible only via secret-manager-admin role; secret read actions are audited and flagged if accessed outside maintenance windows.
- Emergency access: timeboxed Access Requests through PAM system with email + manager approval.

Dedicated:
- Cluster-level admin can be assigned to customer ops team but requires service contract and allowed IP ranges.
- Dedicated pools should have separate instance profiles for system services vs. customer tooling.
- SIEM logs must include pool_id and tenant_id in every event to make lateral movement detection easier.

Private:
- Customer owns host-level access; Redwood ships an agent that emits normalized audit events to customer SIEM or to Redwood-managed collector (optional).
- Recommend customers implement host FIM and log collection agents with centralized retention policy.

Audit log schema (canonical JSON event)
- Purpose: ensure events from hosted, dedicated, and private deployments share a minimal set of attributes so SIEM correlation and evidence automation can function with the same parsers.
- Required fields (all events):
  - timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
  - event_id: UUIDv4
  - env: hosted|dedicated|private
  - tenant_id: short string (or "system" for infra events)
  - principal: user|service name (email or service id)
  - principal_type: human|service|admin
  - action: canonical action string (e.g., "model.deploy", "secret.read", "node.exec")
  - resource: canonical resource id (e.g., "model:abc123")
  - outcome: success|failure|denied
  - src_ip: IPv4/IPv6 (if applicable)
  - request_id: correlation id forwarded through the stack
  - raw_payload: raw event blob (base64) - optional but helpful for forensics

- Optional fields (recommended):
  - change_request_id: link to approval ticket when action was via elevated access
  - escalation_scope: name of access request or incident
  - user_agent: client string
  - geo: {country, region} (stringified for SIEM)

Sample event (single-line JSON for SIEM ingestion):
{"timestamp":"2026-02-09T18:32:12Z","event_id":"0e7b4f6a-9f5a-4c3e-9a2c-1a4d7f0b9c5e","env":"dedicated","tenant_id":"cust-197","principal":"ops@cust.co","principal_type":"human","action":"node.exec","resource":"node:i-08f3","outcome":"success","src_ip":"203.0.113.42","request_id":"req-5c9d2","raw_payload":"..."}

SIEM export mappings and transport options
- Preferred format: JSON over TLS to an ingestion endpoint (either our collector or customer SIEM) with newline-delimited JSON for bulk.
- Alternate: syslog (RFC5424) with structured-data key/value pairs that map to the canonical fields above. Use a consistent tag: REDWOOD-AUDIT.
- Delivery guarantees: events MUST be acked by the endpoint; where possible use persistent queues (Kafka / Kinesis) with replay windows of 7 days.
- Field mapping guidance: keep canonical field names as-is; if the SIEM requires different names, implement a lightweight transform in the collector and preserve orig_* prefixed fields.

Evidence automation and playbook steps
- Audit evidence types we automate: role membership lists, policy versions, access request logs, historical canary approvals, secret-access audit trails, infra change tickets.
- Automation pattern:
  1) Trigger: auditor requests or periodic compliance run.
  2) Query: call internal APIs to collect role membership and policy artifacts (include policy_hmac to prove immutability).
  3) Correlate: join access events with change request ids and review approvals.
  4) Package: create ZIP with JSON manifests, CSV role matrices, and redacted logs.
  5) Sign & publish: sign package with platform key and store in long-term evidence bucket with retention metadata.

- Example implementation notes:
  - Use lambda-style workers to fetch data in parallel and assemble artifacts.
  - Include a small human-readable manifest that maps artifacts to compliance controls (SOC2 CC6.1 etc.).
  - Build in automatic PII redaction filters for logs destined to external auditors.

Operational considerations and SLOs
- SIEM ingestion latency: target <= 60s from action to first-byte in the SIEM for hosted production critical events (inference control plane, secret accesses).
- Audit evidence generation time: best-effort < 2 hours for most artifact bundles; escalate to 24 hours for large historical reconstructions.
- Alerting: anomalous role changes, secret accesses outside windows, and requests from new geo locations generate high-priority incidents.

Testing and validation checklist (short)
- [ ] Policy templates loaded into staging with smoke tests that verify deny rules.
- [ ] SIEM ingestion pipeline validated with synthetic events that include edge-case fields (long resource IDs, absent src_ip).
- [ ] Evidence automation runbook executed monthly and results reviewed by security ops.
- [ ] Red-team exercise to attempt lateral movement across tenant boundaries in dedicated pools.

Common pitfalls and how to avoid them
- Mixing envs in alerts: ensure every log includes env and tenant_id early in the processing pipeline.
- Shadow-roles: audit service-account-to-human mappings annually; prefer ephemeral bindings.
- Silent failures in export: require end-to-end telemetry (heartbeats + sequence numbers) on collectors.

Appendix - quick policy checklist by environment
- Hosted: deny host access, short-lived service tokens, log all secret reads, require manager approval for canary-approver additions.
- Dedicated: restrict admin IPs, require contract + allowlist for cluster-admins, emit pool_id on every event.
- Private: provide canonical event schema; require customer to declare retention and FIM controls in onboarding questionnaire.

Next steps and action items (owners)
- Aisha: create canonical Terraform module for hosted service principal template (ETA: 2026-03-01).
- Leo: add SIEM JSON parser and tests to central collector repo (ETA: 2026-02-24).
- Rina: draft customer-facing onboarding checklist for private deployments (ETA: 2026-03-10).

Questions and open items
- Decide whether to make raw_payload mandatory for dedicated events (tradeoff: storage vs forensics).
- Define retention baseline for hosted vs dedicated audit logs across regions.

End of playbook
